issues.description: Interface name mismatch: the exercise description and template expect an interface named 'Milkable' with method messageOnMilk(), but the solution repository defines the interface as 'Dairy' (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Dairy.java) and leaves solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java empty. This makes it unclear which interface students should implement and causes compilation errors (e.g., solution classes implement 'Dairy' while the template/Main and problem statement reference 'Milkable').
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across all artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (file -> solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java), ensure it declares String messageOnMilk(); remove or repurpose the currently empty Milkable.java file, and update Seal.java and Goat.java to implement Milkable. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to use 'Dairy' instead of 'Milkable' (less recommended). Ensure all references and imports reflect the chosen name so code and instructions are consistent and compile.

issues.description: The concept is the interface for animals that can be milked (method messageOnMilk()). The problem statement (and UML) refer to this interface as 'Milkable' and the template's Main.java uses 'Milkable'. However, the solution repository defines this interface as 'Dairy' (file Dairy.java) and the concrete classes (Seal.java, Goat.java) implement Dairy. There is also an empty Milkable.java file in the solution. This inconsistent identifier naming for the same conceptual entity (milkable/milking interface) makes it unclear which interface students should implement/use and breaks the direct mapping between the exercise description and the provided solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across all artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the solution's interface Dairy to Milkable (Dairy.java -> Milkable.java) and update Goat.java and Seal.java to implement Milkable; remove the empty Milkable.java file from the solution. Alternatively, if 'Dairy' is intended, update the problem statement, UML, and template to use 'Dairy' consistently. Ensure the interface declares String messageOnMilk() so it matches the exercise requirements.
